subject: Verizon Small Cell Antenna Applications
overview: The committee held a public hearing on 44 applications from Verizon for small cell wireless installations on existing utility poles across Medford. The committee established standard conditions for approvals and granted the first application before continuing the remainder of the hearing to a later date.

items.title: Verizon Technical and Safety Presentation
items.summary: Verizon representatives and a physics expert presented on the technical necessity of small cells for 5G coverage and the federal legal framework that prohibits municipalities from denying applications based on health concerns. They argued the non-ionizing radiation levels are well below FCC safety limits and that the installations are designed to improve local network capacity.

items.title: General Public Comment
items.summary: Councilor Michael Marks and numerous residents expressed strong opposition, citing concerns over long-term health effects, property values, and the visual impact of equipment on residential streets. A few speakers supported the applications, emphasizing the need for digital equity and improved internet access for remote work and education.

items.title: 287 Main Street (Application 3)
items.summary: The committee granted the application for utility pole 4136 with standard conditions.

items.title: Standard Conditions for Approval
items.summary: The committee voted to adopt a set of standard conditions for any granted applications, including requirements for professional engineering certifications, radio frequency affidavits, and updated insurance. Additional conditions require Verizon to pay for any infrastructure relocation, prohibit installations on double poles, and ensure noise levels are not detectable to the human ear.

items.title: Hearing Continuance
items.summary: The committee voted to continue the hearing for the remaining 43 applications to April 8, 2021, at 6:30 p.m. due to the length of the proceedings.
